title: Attachments and media
lede: What you can attach, where, and the ceilings that will stop you.

blocks.text: Attachments work at two levels. An **assessment-level** attachment is available to the student for the whole exam — a formulary, a lab reference sheet, a case study. It is set on the Assessment Options page, the student reaches it at any time through the **Exam Controls** menu in Examplify, and you get **exactly one** of them per assessment. A **question-level** attachment is only reachable while the student is on that question, and a question can carry more than one.

blocks.title: One file at assessment level
blocks.text: If your exam needs several shared references, they have to be combined into a single file — typically one PDF — because the assessment accepts only one. Plan that before the draft deadline rather than discovering it during OME proofing.

blocks.title: 200 MB total per assessment
blocks.text: The ceiling covers all attachments **and inline images** in the assessment combined, not each file. A question bank heavy with high-resolution anatomy images will hit this. If you are building an image-dense exam, budget for it early rather than discovering it at the draft deadline.

blocks.title: Where these numbers come from
blocks.text: Images, audio, and video limits are confirmed by both the OME onboarding documents and the vendor article. The PDF and RTF limits come from the vendor article only — the OME documents never listed them. Treat them as accurate but unexercised at JABSOM.

items: Downscale images to the 1920 x 1080 ceiling before uploading. An oversized file is rejected rather than resized.
Radiology and histology images are the usual reason an exam approaches the 200 MB ceiling. Compress rather than crop if diagnostic detail matters.
Video in a secure exam is delivered on the device. Test it on an iPad during OME preview — do not assume desktop playback is representative.
